newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: London robustas to follow New York, seen up US$50.
newsitem.headline: London robustas to follow New York, seen up US$50.

text.p: London robusta futures are seen opening at least US$50 higher later on Tuesday, taking their cue from New York arabicas which jumped to a six-week high yesterday, dealers said.
"I think it will follow New York, but at a slower pace. It should be $50 up," a coffee dealer in Singapore said.
Another trader for a coffee trading house said London should climb by nearly $150 on the numbers.
"But maximum, it should only be $50 higher," the trader said.

The benchmark September contract in London finished $25 up on Monday at $1,615 a tonne after touching a session high of $1,619. September arabicas on the other hand soared 12.50 U.S. cents up yesterday to close at 188.35 cents/lb.
New York coffee dealers said worries over a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract fuelled the rally.
The Asian coffee business was fairly active, but dealers said supplies of Indonesian beans remain tight.
"Business is good, but the problem is finding the beans. Supply has been a bit tight," one dealer said.
Indonesia's key Grade 4 coffee, 80 defects, was quoted by the trade at around $70 under to level money, basis the September robusta contract in London.
